detail.longDescription: All I have found in the documentation is: The default bin size is determined using a reference rule that depends on the sample size and variance. I calculated the bin width based on the Freedman-Diaconis rule for a histogram, which suggests that the bin="auto" indicates a different method. What method? import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import seaborn as sns import numpy as np # Calculate the optimal number of bins according to Freedman and Diaconis width = 2 * (np.percentile(data, 75) - np.percentile(data, 25)) * len(data)**(-1/3) print(width) n = (max(data) - min(data)) / width print("n = ", n) sns.histplot(data, kde=True, bins=np.round(int(n), decimals=0), label=r"$t_{CP}$", alpha=.6) sns.histplot(data, kde=True, bins='auto', label=r"$t_{CP}$", alpha=.6) plt.legend(frameon=False) plt.show()
